Country.evidence_source: Charity S. Akotia, Department of Psychology, School of Social Sciences, University of Ghana, Legon, Accra, Ghana. The consequence of such stigma and criminalization of attempted suicide in Ghana presents a serious challenge to the health care system leading to underreporting and poor recording (Adinkrah, 2010, 2012). Suicide research in Ghana has burgeoned in recent years but there are still no accurate statistics available (Knizek, Akotia, & Hjelmeland, 2010; Osafo et al., 2015b; Osafo et al., 2011a; Osafo, Knizek, Akotia, & Hjelmeland, 2011b). The purpose of this study therefore was to investigate the reasons for attempting suicide as expressed by people who have attempted suicide in Ghana.

We chose the term ''reasons'' and not ''causes'' to represent this (Hjelmeland & Knizek, 1999) because we focused on participants' own explanations of their actions.
